meta.title: Rig management — see the machine, place the Core
meta.description: PLAN (0.7). Settings gains a Rig section: a SvelteFlow graph of the machine. HARDWARE nodes are illustrated cards — one per detected GPU, plus CPU, RAM and the disk or NAS the weights live on. WORKLOAD nodes are the things that run — the Core, the embedder, crv, Typesense, anything else found on a card. EDGES say where each workload loads and runs. Three layers are kept apart: OBSERVED (the driver, now), NEXT START (profile defaults + cores.d overrides), DRAFT (a what-if being edited). A layout is only a parameter change written through the existing overrides path; the harness still never runs systemctl — the park watchdog applies it. A fit estimator answers 'does this model fit this layout, and with how much context' from local checkpoint facts or Hugging Face. Scoped on purpose: the rest of Cerveau is in Architecture, the Core internals in profile-*.

frames.label: Panel · Settings, revamped
frames.note: Svelte 5. Settings.svelte is a 762-line monolith today (Engine · Sound · RFX in one scroll); it becomes a shell with a section nav and one file per section.

frames.label: crv · Go core · new internal/rig
frames.note: New package internal/rig plus one handler file. Everything that WRITES goes through the existing internal/cores — rig adds description and arithmetic, never a second way to change a Core.

frames.label: State · what decides placement
frames.note: All existing except the rig cache. A layout is a diff in cores.d; nothing new becomes a source of truth.

frames.label: Machine · what actually runs
frames.note: Owned by systemd, not by Cerveau. The harness never runs systemctl — that invariant is why a crash mid-switch cannot strand the machine with no model.

nodes.label: Settings shell
nodes.sublabel: icon tabs: Rig · Engine · Generation · Talents · Sound — one section on screen
nodes.note: A ~100-line shell and one file per section, each owning its own loading. Tabs are an icon and a word, selected the way everything in the panel is (raised surface + accent hairline + accent icon), with the open section's one-line description at the right. The open section is remembered. Forms sit in a 640 px column; Rig takes the full width. vocabulary.ts is the ONE place a profile's parameters are put into words (label · reading · tip): the Engine table and the Rig spec plate both read it, and a key it does not know is still shown under its own name.

nodes.label: Rig diagram
nodes.sublabel: a FIXED SvelteFlow diagram: hardware cards · workload cards · links you draw
nodes.note: A fixed diagram: pan, zoom and scroll are off; the frame takes the drawing's own aspect ratio; the legend sits on the diagram. Draws whichever profile the head has chosen. ONE effect, keyed on the profile on screen, drops every draft and plan when that profile changes — by the user's pick or because another device switched the live Core under an open page — and opens the engine card's form. A plan is saved only to the profile it names (found in review 2026-09-20: a draft for profile A could otherwise be saved over profile B after a poll). Link colour = its module's; stroke = state. ROOT-CAUSE FIX on record: tokens.css gave every svg max-width:100%, collapsing SvelteFlow's edge svgs — `.svelte-flow svg { max-width: none }`.

nodes.label: Linking
nodes.sublabel: drag a module's port onto a card · click a link to remove it
nodes.note: BUILT inside the diagram rather than as a separate editor: the Core and the embedder carry a visible port; the whole hardware card is the drop target (a link is aimed at 'that GPU', not at a 6px dot). While a link is in the air, cards that can take it light up in accent and the ones that cannot fade (rigLink store), and existing links step back. The embedder taken off its card goes to the CPU — it is never left nowhere. Every change round-trips POST /api/rig/plan; the panel does no placement arithmetic. SvelteFlow's automatic edge is declined in onbeforeconnect, because links are derived from the placement. Presets (spread · pack · leave N free) are NOT built yet.

nodes.label: Model fit browser
nodes.sublabel: search Hugging Face · does it fit this layout, with how much context
nodes.note: A what-if tool first: search, pick a model, see fits / tight / does not fit per layout and the largest context that fits. It does NOT download or install a model in this plan — installing a profile stays install.sh's job.

nodes.label: rig.svelte.ts
nodes.sublabel: inventory · live stats · allocation · draft layout
nodes.note: BUILT: /api/rig every 5 s (two nvidia-smi calls a time), /api/system/stats every 2 s, both only while the Rig section is mounted. Keeps the last good picture through a failed poll; reports 'unsupported' when the core never answers /api/rig.

nodes.label: api.ts
nodes.sublabel: typed client — components never string-build URLs
nodes.note: Gains rig functions + Rig* types. The existing cores functions (params, apply) are reused unchanged.

ports.shape: GET /api/rig → {inventory, observed[], next, services[]} · POST /api/rig/plan {core, gpus[], embed} → {overrides, embed_overrides, changed[], fit, problems[]} · GET /api/rig/models?q= → model facts[] · POST /api/rig/fit {model, layout} → verdict

nodes.label: /api/rig/*
nodes.sublabel: GET rig · POST plan · GET models · POST fit
nodes.note: Thin handlers: every rule is in internal/rig. GET /api/rig[?core=] (profile resolved BEFORE the driver is touched) → {inventory, observed[], next{…params, live}, profiles[]} · POST /api/rig/plan {core, gpus, embed, gpu_util} → Plan + fit · GET|PUT|DELETE /api/rig/layouts (the two that write take JSON only, like every endpoint a sandboxed panel must not reach). Still TODO: the Hugging Face model browser.

nodes.label: rig/inventory
nodes.sublabel: what the machine HAS: GPUs, VRAM, PCIe, power cap, link topology
nodes.note: Static GPU facts from one nvidia-smi query plus `topo -m` for the link matrix (this rig: all NODE, no NVLink). Cached in memory for a minute — the cards do not change while the panel is open. No nvidia-smi → empty list, a CPU-only box, not an error. CPU and RAM are NOT duplicated here: /api/system/stats already reports their name, core count, size, type and speed, and the rig store reads them from there.

nodes.label: rig/alloc
nodes.sublabel: who is USING what: observed per-GPU consumers + declared next-start placement
nodes.note: OBSERVED: nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,used_memory, then pid → /proc/<pid>/cgroup → systemd unit, so VRAM is attributed to 'the Core', 'the embedder' or 'other' without guessing from names (vLLM's TP workers are children in the Core unit's cgroup). DECLARED: the active Core's effective params (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, TP, GPU_UTIL, KV, MAX_LEN) and effective embed placement. Both are returned; the panel shows the difference instead of hiding it.

nodes.label: rig/estimate
nodes.sublabel: weights ÷ TP + KV for the window + overhead, per card → fits / tight / no
nodes.note: BUILT, 7 tests on the rig's real numbers. Per card: share of the card = weights ÷ cards + ~2.5 GB runtime + room for KV. One token costs a card 2 × attention layers × its KV heads × head dim × (1 byte fp8 | 2 otherwise). Verdict fits · tight · no · unknown, with the reason and the LARGEST window that fits. Also refuses what vLLM would: a card whose FREE memory is below its share because something else holds it. Live: W8A16 on four cards fits with room for 1.6M tokens; on one card the weights alone need 29.4 GB of a 22.1 GB share; BF16 fits with 363K and is flagged as loading 51.7 GB over the NAS.

nodes.label: rig/layout
nodes.sublabel: a drawn layout → the profile's parameter language, validated
nodes.note: PlanLayout(PlanInput, LayoutRequest) → Plan. The plan names the profile it was made for (`core`) and carries the COMPLETE override sets to save (existing overrides + placement keys), because SetCoreParams replaces the file. Always writes CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID. Group sizes come from the model's head counts (facts), powers of two when the checkpoint cannot be read. The embedder's room beside the Core is what it is MEASURED to hold (+25%) when it is running, a 3 GB default otherwise. Refuses: an illegal group size, a share outside 20–98%, the embedder on a card the Core fills, unknown cards, a profile with no placement keys (rig.Placeable — one definition, used by Declared, PlanLayout and the profile list). layouts.go is 'Save as': named placements per profile in rig-layouts.json, at most 24 each.

flags.title: Only the two TP=4 profiles declare placement params — llama.cpp and the single-card vLLM Core expose none
flags.note: Checked the installed cores.json: vllm-27b-bf16 and vllm-27b-w8a16 declare CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, TP, GPU_UTIL, KV, MAX_LEN, MODEL. The `llamacpp` Core (cerveau-llama.service) and the older `vllm` Core have an empty params map, so there is nothing for a layout to write. llama.cpp also speaks a different language: --tensor-split, -ngl, --n-cpu-moe rather than TP. And the vLLM launcher that turns env into flags lives outside this repo (Gpu-Rig/quad/start_qwen_tp4.sh), so the contract is not enforced here.
flags.fix: Define one small placement contract per engine — vLLM: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES + TP + GPU_UTIL; llama.cpp: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES + TENSOR_SPLIT + N_CPU_MOE — and have rig/layout pick the adapter from core.engine. A Core that declares none of the keys is shown read-only on the canvas ('this profile does not expose placement') instead of offering an editor that cannot save. Decide whether 0.7 ships the llama.cpp adapter or vLLM only.

nodes.label: rig/hf
nodes.sublabel: Hugging Face Hub: search · model info · config.json
nodes.note: GET /api/models?search=…&pipeline_tag=text-generation, GET /api/models/{id} (safetensors parameter totals by dtype, sibling file sizes), and config.json for layers / KV heads / head dim / quantization_config. Facts are cached on disk so a model looked up once can be re-evaluated offline.

flags.title: A model browser sends search terms to huggingface.co — against 'no cloud, no accounts, no telemetry'
flags.note: Checked the Go core's outbound hosts: the only one it contacts on its own is dl.typesense.org, once, when the user installs the memory sidecar. Everything else is the user's own services or a tool the user/model invoked (web_fetch, the GitHub pack). A model browser would be the first feature where using Settings sends what the user typed to a third party. For the labs and clinics this is built for, that must be a visible choice, not a side effect of opening a panel.
flags.fix: User-initiated only: a request goes out when the user presses Search or opens a model, never on load, never in the background, no refresh timer. A config switch turns the browser off entirely, and the panel then offers 'paste a repo id or a local model path' — a local config.json + safetensors sizes give the same facts with no network. An HF token is optional, read from the environment for gated repos, never stored in the rig cache and never logged. Cached facts keep working offline.

nodes.note: Exists and already reports every GPU, plus the CPU name/cores and RAM size/type/speed the canvas needs. Reused as is.

The Engine tab shows the refusal instead of failing silently.

nodes.label: crv-park-watchdog
nodes.sublabel: polls the switch request · stops the other Cores · starts this one · restarts Cerveau

flags.title: The switch waits for EVERY card to be empty — a layout that leaves things on other cards stalls each switch for 60 s
flags.note: crv-park-watchdog.sh, switch_core: after stopping the old Core it loops up to 30 × 2 s until no compute process anywhere holds more than 2000 MiB (`nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=used_memory | awk '$1>2000'`). It does not look at WHICH card or WHOSE process. Rig management exists to let the Core take cards 2 and 3 while the embedder and other work stay on 0, 1 and 4 — every one of those layouts makes the loop run its full minute before the Core even starts loading. The embedder alone can cross 2 GB.
flags.fix: Put the new Core's card group in the switch request (`gpus`, as UUIDs from the inventory) and have the watchdog wait only for those cards: --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,used_memory filtered to the group. Still bounded, still proceeds on timeout. One field in SwitchRequest, one awk filter.

nodes.note: Environment= defaults, then EnvironmentFile=-cores.d/<id>.env which wins. The two TP=4 profiles declare everything a layout needs: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, TP, GPU_UTIL, KV, MAX_LEN, MODEL.

nodes.label: rigGraph.ts
nodes.sublabel: rig data → flow nodes + edges + positions · pure, table-tested
nodes.note: BUILT, 12 vitest cases from the lab rig's real /api/rig output: five cards, one card, no GPU, Core parked, Core running, observed ≠ next start in both directions, embedder on CPU, a docker container found on every card, the desktop's memory shown as 'system'. Places each workload above the middle of what it runs on and pushes overlapping cards apart. Storage (nvme · sata · hdd · nas) is NOT drawn yet: nothing reports where the weights live until rig/facts exists, and the graph does not guess.

nodes.label: Node cards
nodes.sublabel: HardwareNode (illustration + live meters) · WorkloadNode (what runs, how much it takes)
nodes.note: HardwareNode: the illustration, the name, a memory bar split by who holds it, temp · load · power; the whole card is the drop target. WorkloadNode: the module's brand mark, title, state, chips, and — for the Core and the embedder — a port to drag from. ONE colour per module (--c, from its brand; the Core keeps the accent): the same on its mark, its card rule, its links and its share of every memory bar.

nodes.label: Component illustrations
nodes.sublabel: GPU · CPU · RAM · NVMe · SATA SSD · HDD · NAS — line-art SVG, every one animated by load
nodes.note: BUILT: seven colourless, timeless SVG files + RigArt.svelte, which inlines one by kind (as EngineMark does the engine logos). Styled by class: b body · p part · v void · d detail · m marker. Moved by class, only while load > 0: fan (GPU, the pair counter-rotates) · platter + seek (HDD: the disk turns, the arm hunts from hub to outer tracks) · lit overlays with a phase --p (CPU pads chase round the package · a wave crosses the RAM packages · NVMe lights controller → cache → flash → flash · SATA level strip + LED · NAS power LED steady, drive LEDs blinking out of step). ONE number drives all of it — load 0–1 sets --dur, a GPU fan's full turn (3 s → 0.6 s); every other motion is a fixed multiple, so the rig speeds up and slows down together. Props: kind, width, load, tone (idle · on · accent — the accent means 'the draft targets this', nothing else). `node scripts/make-rig-art.mjs` regenerates; `--preview` writes docs-private/rig-art-preview.html using the CSS lifted out of RigArt.svelte, so the page cannot drift from the panel. GPU traced from cerveau-site's gpu.glb.

nodes.label: rig/facts
nodes.sublabel: model facts from a LOCAL checkpoint first, Hugging Face second
nodes.note: BUILT. Reads the profile's own MODEL path (%h and ~ expanded): config.json (text_config for multimodal) + the sizes of the weight shards. AttnLayers counts only full-attention layers — Qwen3.5 is a hybrid, 16 of 64: counting all of them overstates the KV cache four times. GroupSizes come from the model's heads (24 attention, 4 KV, 16/48 linear → 1, 2, 4, 8). Remote = the checkpoint is on a network mount (the BF16 weights are on the NAS). A bare GGUF gives a size and nothing else, and the estimate says so. The handler reads it with a 3 s timeout: a stat on a dead SMB share can hang. Hugging Face is NOT wired in: the installed model is evaluated with no network.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.sublabel: the MODEL path: safetensors / GGUF + config.json — on an NVMe, a SATA SSD, a hard drive or a NAS mount
nodes.note: BF16 weights live on the NAS on this rig (see profile-bf16-tp4's open flag): the canvas should show that the Core loads over the network, and say so when the mount is absent.

nodes.label: Profile bar
nodes.sublabel: every profile · live or preview · the chosen one's configuration, read from the profile
nodes.note: BUILT 2026-09-20, replacing a header of hand-written sentences. One button per profile from /api/rig `profiles` (engine mark, name, a 'live' tag on the loaded one). Picking one redraws the diagram for it: REAL TIME if it is the loaded Core, a PREVIEW of where it would go if it is not — and the Core that IS loaded stays on the cards, named. The configuration strip is the profile's effective params said the way a person would ('256K window', 'fp8 KV cache', '92% of each card'); a key it does not know is shown as written, never dropped.

nodes.label: Module form
nodes.sublabel: click a module: where it runs · more · less · none · would it run? · Save · Save as · Cancel
nodes.note: BUILT 2026-09-20 — the user's chosen way to change the graph. Core: a switch per card, the share of each card (− / slider / +), 'Would it run?' with the verdict, the reasons and a per-card table (weights · KV room · window needs), what saving changes, saved layouts, and Save · Save as… · Cancel. Embedder: CPU or one card. Anything else: read-only, saying why. It edits nothing itself: every change goes up as a whole placement, the diagram redraws, and the core answers what it means. Nothing is written until Save.

nodes.label: rig-layouts.json
nodes.sublabel: ~/.config/cerveau — named placements kept beside each profile ('Save as')
nodes.note: A profile is a systemd unit with its own port, so a drawn placement cannot become a NEW profile from the panel. 'Save as' keeps it as a named layout instead; loading one only fills the editor — Save is still what writes the profile.

nodes.label: brands
nodes.sublabel: a module's own strings → its brand's mark and colour · vendored, never fetched
nodes.note: BUILT 2026-09-20. Resolution order: a vendored icon first, else the brand's own site is asked for its vector mark, else a neutral icon. WHEN it runs matters: Cerveau is local-first, so scripts/vendor-brand-icons.mjs runs that resolution at development time (LobeHub MIT → Simple Icons CC0 → the site's own svg → the site's raster icon) and commits the result with its source and licence in brands.json. The panel never goes to the network for a picture. brandFor(...names) takes a module's title, model name, systemd unit and process name and returns the first brand they name — 'nemotron-embed' → NVIDIA, a docker-… scope → Docker whatever runs inside it — or null, and the card draws a neutral box. No component names a brand; adding one is one line in the script. Colours are lifted until legible on #161616. Typesense publishes no vector mark, so it keeps its official PNG, untinted.
